nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

## Model Links
[🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)

**loras**

- 4 steps: [minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/loras/minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors)

**embeddings**

- [10 style embeddings](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/tree/main/embeddings) (`minimaxh3_*.safetensors`), for example `minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

## Model Storage Location

```
📂 ComfyUI/
├── 📂 models/
│   ├── 📂 vae/
│   │   ├── minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
│   │   └── minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 diffusion_models/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 text_encoders/
│   │   └── qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
│   ├── 📂 loras/
│   │   └── minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16.safetensors
│   └── 📂 embeddings/
│       └── minimaxh3_art_is_explosion.safetensors
```

## Using Prompt Embeddings

Prompt embeddings (supported since [ComfyUI#15697](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15697)) add reusable style tokens to your prompt. Download one or more embeddings from the folder above into `ComfyUI/models/embeddings/`, then reference one in the prompt text with the `embedding:` prefix and the filename without its extension, for example:

`embedding:minimaxh3_art_is_explosion`

Using an embedding is optional and the template runs fine without one.

## Report Issue

Note: Please update ComfyUI first ([guide](https://docs.comfy.org/installation/update_comfyui)) and prepare required models. Desktop/Cloud updates follow stable releases, so some nightly-supported models may not be available yet.

- Cannot run / runtime errors: [ComfyUI/issues](https://github.com/comfyanonymous/ComfyUI/issues)
- UI / frontend issues: [ComfyUI_frontend/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI_frontend/issues)
- Workflow issues: [workflow_templates/issues](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/workflow_templates/issues)

<Subject 1> performs exactly the body movements and poses shown in the motion reference video, in the same order and with the same timing and rhythm. The camera stays static, framing the man's full body from head to toe. Simple neutral indoor background with soft natural window light. The man's face, hair, slim build and plain black t-shirt stay identical to <Picture 1> throughout.

# Full-Reference Video Generation Prompt — Rotating Hive Chamber

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the astronaut defined by <Picture 1>: a human figure wearing a sleek white spacesuit with a rigid white helmet, clear visor, white life-support backpack, segmented torso and limb armor, gloves, reinforced knee sections, and heavy white space boots. The astronaut carries a rectangular tablet-like device in one hand. <Picture 1> defines the astronaut’s finished appearance, suit construction, materials, colors, proportions, equipment, and lighting treatment. The astronaut’s walk cycle, stride timing, body mechanics, limb trajectories, weight shifts, tablet-hand movement, and complete pose progression come from <Video 1>.

<Subject 2> is the enormous enclosed hive environment visually defined by <Picture 1>: a claustrophobic organic-industrial passage constructed from dense amber honeycomb cells surrounded by thick dark green-black ribbed structural bands. Golden viscous hive material coats portions of the walls, hangs in elongated drips from overhead surfaces, collects around the lower edges, and forms glossy pools across the dark wet floor. The environment combines recognizable hexagonal hive structures with heavy biomechanical-looking ribs and an enclosed tunnel-like architecture.

<Subject 3> is the giant cylindrical hamster-wheel configuration and coordinated environment rotation taken from <Video 1>. The floor, honeycomb walls, overhead structures, dark ribs, hive surfaces, and all environmental geometry attached to the cylindrical chamber rotate according to the exact direction, angular velocity, acceleration, phase, timing, and spatial relationships established by <Video 1>.

<Subject 4> is the amber viscous hive material defined by <Picture 1>, including long hanging strands, thick droplets, wall coatings, and glossy pooled material. Its appearance remains attached to the rotating hive architecture, with only restrained secondary deformation where physically appropriate; it must not detach from the reference geometry or create independent large-scale motion that interferes with <Video 1>.

<Video 1> is the original untextured 3D animation reference and the authoritative temporal and spatial source for the entire target video. It defines the exact astronaut animation, walking cadence, frame-by-frame poses, environment rotation, background movement, camera angle, camera position, framing, tracking behavior, lens behavior, shot duration, and complete temporal progression. Whenever movement implied by <Picture 1> differs from <Video 1>, <Video 1> takes absolute priority.

<Picture 1> is the finished visual reference for the target rendering, defining <Subject 1>, the honeycomb hive architecture of <Subject 2>, the amber-and-dark-green material palette, viscous organic material, wet reflective surfaces, lighting relationships, atmospheric depth, and overall cinematic rendering style.

summary:
[reference generation] The target video recreates the exact rotating hamster-wheel animation and camera performance of <Video 1> while applying the finished astronaut and hive-world appearance established by <Picture 1>. <Subject 1> performs the identical frame-by-frame walking animation from <Video 1>, while <Subject 3> causes the entire honeycomb chamber—floor, walls, ceiling, ribs, and hive structures—to revolve continuously around and beneath the astronaut. The fundamental effect remains unchanged: the astronaut walks toward camera while the enormous enclosed hive tunnel endlessly rolls around its central axis. <Video 1> has absolute priority for character movement, timing, environmental rotation, blocking, camera motion, and framing.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (throughout [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - the finished white astronaut appearance and tablet from <Picture 1> are transferred onto the animated character from <Video 1> while preserving the source pose sequence, stride mechanics, body motion, timing, orientation, and spatial trajectory.
<Subject 2> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the amber honeycomb cells, dark green-black structural ribs, enclosed organic architecture, glossy wet surfaces, and hive material from <Picture 1> define the finished environment.
<Subject 3> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the revolving floor, walls, ceiling, hive structures, background geometry, angular direction, speed, phase, and synchronization follow <Video 1> exactly.
<Subject 4> (throughout [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the amber viscous material retains its thick glossy appearance and remains spatially associated with the rotating hive surfaces.
<Video 1> (entire temporal structure): fully_preserved - preserve its complete animation, timing, camera transform, camera angle, framing, environment rotation, shot duration, and frame progression without alteration.
<Picture 1> (finished character/environment reference): partially_preserved - its astronaut, hive architecture, honeycomb design, dark structural ribs, amber slime, wet surfaces, lighting, and cinematic appearance are preserved while the architecture follows the cylindrical rotating configuration dictated by <Video 1>.

detailed_description:
The target video is a highly detailed cinematic 3D CG science-fiction hive sequence combining the finished visual treatment of <Picture 1> with the exact animation and virtual-camera performance of <Video 1>. The central effect is the giant rotating hamster-wheel room: the astronaut continuously walks toward camera while the entire honeycomb-lined cylindrical hive rotates around and underneath the astronaut. <Video 1> is the strict motion master; no movement should be regenerated from the still image.

[Shot 1] Reproduce the complete continuous shot from <Video 1> at identical duration and timing. Replace the original blockout character with <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>. Preserve the white helmet and clear visor, segmented white pressure suit, backpack, gloves, articulated leg protection, heavy boots, and handheld rectangular tablet. Every step follows <Video 1> frame for frame: foot placement, planted-foot duration, heel-to-toe transition, knee articulation, hip displacement, torso counter-rotation, shoulder motion, arm trajectory, hand position, helmet movement, vertical rise and fall, balance correction, and complete pose progression remain unchanged.

The tablet stays associated with the corresponding hand and follows that hand’s exact reference trajectory. Do not alter the astronaut’s arm animation to make the tablet more visible, and do not add scanning, typing, looking-down, or interface interactions unless they already occur in <Video 1>.

Transform the complete surrounding chamber into <Subject 2>. Large amber honeycomb structures densely cover the cylindrical interior, separated and reinforced by thick dark green-black organic ribs that curve around the tunnel. Hexagonal cavities vary naturally in depth and scale while remaining visually consistent with <Picture 1>. Golden-brown viscous material coats sections of the hive, stretches downward from overhead surfaces, and gathers into thick glossy deposits around structural seams. The walkable surface is dark, wet, and reflective, catching subdued amber highlights from the surrounding hive.

The complete architectural volume performs <Subject 3>'s rotation exactly as established by <Video 1>. The floor revolves beneath the astronaut while both honeycomb-covered side walls continuously roll around the chamber's central longitudinal axis. The ceiling simultaneously participates in the same rotation. This must read unmistakably as one enormous cylindrical room rotating like a hamster wheel around the walking astronaut.

Use distinctive honeycomb clusters and large dark ribs as rotational landmarks. A recognizable cluster beginning on one side of the frame progressively travels downward toward floor level, rotates underneath the astronaut, rises along the opposite side, and eventually passes overhead according to the exact angular progression in <Video 1>. Likewise, individual structural ribs travel continuously around the circumference rather than remaining fixed in screen space.

Every part of the hive architecture is physically locked to the rotating cylinder. Honeycomb cells, dark ribs, wall textures, structural seams, pooled deposits, and attached <Subject 4> material rotate together. Do not animate the walls independently from the floor, do not slide texture patterns over stationary geometry, and do not create a stationary corridor with only superficial background motion.

<Subject 4> follows the same rotational attachment. Amber strands hanging from a surface remain connected to that particular surface as its orientation changes around the cylinder. Their shapes may respond subtly to motion and gravity, but this secondary response must remain restrained. Do not create large splashes, detached blobs, falling masses, or excessive dripping unless such events are explicitly animated in <Video 1>. The primary readable motion must always be the reference chamber rotation.

Lighting follows the visual hierarchy of <Picture 1>. The astronaut remains the brightest central figure against the darker green-black hive architecture. Warm amber light passes through and reflects from the honeycomb structures, producing subdued golden highlights on the astronaut's white suit and moving reflections across the wet floor. Because the environment rotates, these highlights and reflections naturally change as illuminated hive surfaces move around the astronaut.

The astronaut does not rotate with the room unless <Video 1> explicitly contains such body rotation. Preserve the exact relationship between the walking character, the moving contact surface beneath the boots, and the rotating architectural cylinder. Do not procedurally modify foot placement to compensate for the unusual environment.

The camera reproduces <Video 1> exactly. Preserve the same frontal low-angle viewpoint, camera height, distance, pitch, yaw, roll, focal perspective, tracking behavior, subject scale, and framing. Do not add a camera roll merely to emphasize the hamster-wheel effect, do not stabilize the rotating environment beyond the source camera behavior, and do not automatically recenter the astronaut. Camera motion must remain frame-accurate to <Video 1>.

The target ends on precisely the same astronaut pose, walking phase, environmental rotational phase, camera transform, framing, and animation endpoint as <Video 1>. Do not append an extra step, additional rotation, slowdown, freeze-frame, fade, or transition.

overall_soundscape:
Heavy muted spacesuit footsteps contact the wet rotating surface in exact synchronization with <Video 1>, accompanied by restrained suit articulation, fabric movement, and subtle equipment sounds. A deep enclosed organic-mechanical rumble follows the continuous rotation of the massive hive cylinder, layered with occasional structural creaks, sticky viscous movement, isolated thick drips, and distant resonant hive ambience.
